name: drag-scrub-bar-seeks
description: Dragging the scrub bar with the mouse seeks, where setting its value does not - the two reach the core by different paths.

steps.note: Pause first so the position cannot race past the assertion.

Press at the left edge and slide to three quarters. ScrubBar is a self-painting RangeSlider with no child handle, so a drag can only work if its own press/move/release handling runs - which is the path set_value deliberately does not take.
Bounded settle so the exact seek lands before the synchronous core read. The assertion below carries the scenario; this is not a synchroniser.

assertions.note: Pins the constant the next assertion is computed from, so a fixture or load fault reports as its own failure instead of quietly invalidating the expected 9.0.
Three quarters of a 12.000s fixture. A build whose scrub bar ignored the drag leaves time-pos at the start and fails here.
The widget followed the pointer, not just the core. A build that seeked the core without moving the control would pass the time-pos assertion and fail this one.
